title: OODA Loop Framework Genome

identity.name: OODA Loop (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act)
identity.first_documented: conflicting — the decision-cycle concept was presented in briefings from 1976 onward, but Boyd's only self-drawn diagram of the full loop dates to 1995-1996

purpose.stated: Operate inside an adversary's decision cycle by observing, orienting, deciding, and acting faster and more effectively than the opponent, producing confusion and an inability to cope in the opponent.
purpose.scope_claimed: conflicting — Boyd's own briefings address air combat and military strategy; secondary authors (not verified in this execution beyond citation identification) extend the claimed scope to business, litigation, and general decision-making.

structure.central_element: Orient is reported as receiving substantially more internal elaboration than the other three stages in Boyd's own 1995/1996 diagram (e.g., cultural background, prior experience, new information, analysis/synthesis feeding into it).
structure.diagram_provenance: conflicting/uncertain — the widely reproduced simplified four-box cyclical diagram is not Boyd's own drawing; Boyd's only known self-authored sketch is reported to be more elaborate and is specific to the 1995/1996 briefing.

reasoning.logic: not-reported as a formal decision logic within the primary briefings themselves; secondary analysis (Osinga) situates Boyd's broader theory within epistemology, thermodynamics/entropy, and evolutionary-biology analogies rather than a stated formal algorithm.
reasoning.decision_rule: not-reported — no explicit decision rule or algorithm for the Decide step is documented in the sources reviewed.

operation.sequence: Commonly presented as a repeating Observe-Orient-Decide-Act cycle, but Boyd's own diagram is reported to include feed-forward and feedback paths (e.g., Orient feeding directly into Act, outputs feeding back into Observe/Orient) rather than a strict single-direction loop.
operation.tempo_claim: Sources report the strategic aim as cycling through the stages faster than an adversary ('getting inside' the opponent's loop), not merely completing the cycle.
operation.cadence: not-reported — no fixed timing, frequency, or duration is specified.

human_system.intended_users: conflicting/broadened over time — originally framed around individual fighter pilots and military commanders; later secondary literature (not independently verified here) extends this to organizations and other decision-makers.
human_system.roles: not-reported beyond an undifferentiated decision-maker/commander in the primary briefings reviewed.
human_system.facilitation: not-reported — no facilitator, workshop, or group process is specified; the briefings describe individual/organizational cognition rather than a facilitated method.

adaptation.guidance: not-reported — the primary briefings reviewed do not provide explicit instructions for tailoring the loop to new domains.
adaptation.contested_extensions: conflicting — a secondary critical source argues the model's vagueness is precisely what permits broad reinterpretation, treating this as a weakness rather than a documented adaptation mechanism.

risk.reported_limitations: A secondary critical source argues the concept is vague enough that both defenders and critics read into it what they want, and separately disputes a commonly cited ~10:1 Korean War F-86-vs-MiG-15 kill ratio used in some Boyd-derived commentary as empirical support.
risk.primary_source_risk_disclosure: not-reported — the primary briefings reviewed do not themselves enumerate failure modes or misuse conditions.

evidence.note: FE-SRC-OODA-005 (Wikipedia) is tertiary and was used only to orient the search and locate the other sources; no dimension claim above relies on it alone.

limitations: Primary briefings (FE-SRC-OODA-001, FE-SRC-OODA-002) were bibliographically identified but not fetched and read in full text for this execution; claims attributed to them are limited to what is corroborated by secondary-source summaries or search-result excerpts.
No independent second-provider execution has yet reviewed or replicated this Genome.
This Genome does not assess or imply that any dimension is beneficial; presence of a property is not evidence of effectiveness.
